01

What was done—and what the evidence supports

Two independent oomycete datasets were screened for non-target sequences, followed by reference mapping, targeted specificity checks, and assembly-based visualisation. The completed runs include both de novo DNA assembly and de novo RNA transcript assembly.

Main finding: the pilot Pseudomonas CIP-10 assignment was not independently validated. Its retained support was dominated by structural RNA regions; broader searches offered oomycete/eukaryotic alternatives. This does not prove every read is host-derived, nor establish a database error.

These are different species and isolates, not matched DNA and RNA from one organism. Shared screening labels cannot demonstrate a shared infection or associate.

Additional assembly-only dataset

Globisporangium irregulare strain 13-30, GCA_051997085.1; PRJNA816194; SAMN26664723; WGS JALBZS000000000; taxid 36331. Input: 5,451 sequences, 42,653,821 bp. Selected because the user reports NCBI flagged the genome as contaminated; exact flag wording was not independently retrieved. This independent FCS-GX case is not either SRA readset above. No associated SRA run was verified and no raw reads from this genome were analysed. See the FCS-GX case section for findings and all dataset metadata.

03

Analysis flow

SRA runs
prefetch → validation → paired FASTQ
↓
FastQC + fastp
full cleaned paired readsets
↓
100,000 pairs per sample
seed 1729 → Kraken2 → candidate review
↓
Candidate-only and competitive mapping
Bowtie2 + SAMtools → read fraction, depth, breadth
↓
Specificity audit
rRNA/tRNA annotations + selected-pair NCBI BLAST

Parallel abundance comparison

Same subsamples → pluspf Kraken2 → Bracken (DNA 150 bp; RNA 100 bp approximation).

Assembly branches

Published DNA genome + full DNA reads; SPAdes DNA contigs; rnaSPAdes transcripts → read mapping + contig Kraken labels → native BlobToolKit data and R figures.

Genome assembly and transcript assembly used the full cleaned reads, not the screening subsamples. RNA strandedness was left unknown rather than guessed. Assembly coverage is mapped per-base depth, not the k-mer coverage printed in SPAdes headers.

Kraken2 was run with confidence 0.1. Paired classification counts represent fragments/spots. Most reads were unclassified against these databases; this alone does not establish their biological origin or prove target-genome absence from an index.

The original database and pluspf are distinct. The much larger nt_database index was not used. Database release/taxonomy provenance remain unknown where records do not establish them. No new database was downloaded.

Candidate filters: MAPQ ≥20; unavailable MAPQ255 excluded; primary, non-QC-failed, non-flagged-duplicate alignments; base quality ≥0. Depth removes overlapping mates and includes zero-depth positions across all reference contigs. No duplicate marking was performed. Fragments count distinct read-pair names with either mate supporting a reference; do not sum across discordant reference assignments. RNA host competition used a genomic reference, so splice-spanning reads are a limitation.

Full TSV · CSV · Column definitions. RNA round-two measurements replace the earlier pilot rows in the final table; earlier runs remain separately retained.

06

Why the Pseudomonas pilot was not validated

AssayCompetitive readsSupporting fragmentsrRNA-overlapping readsRemaining support
DNA1431161430 outside annotated rRNA
RNA1281151261 tRNA-overlapping read; 1 sucD read

The rRNA-overlapping alignments fall on CP087163.1, an 8,012 bp record labelled plasmid unnamed3 with annotated 16S, 23S, 5S and partial 16S features. Annotation overlap does not mean every base of a read lies within that feature. The label alone does not establish a genuine plasmid or a database error.

The remaining RNA chromosome alignments overlapped tRNA-Gln and sucD. Both mates of the sucD pair matched Phytophthora transcripts; the displayed mate-1 hits included 93.33% identity across 90 bp, and mate 2 matched 64/90 bp at 93.75% identity. Representative rRNA pairs matched oomycete and other eukaryotic references at high identity, often across the full read. Short conserved matches labelled plant, moss or other taxa are not independent evidence that those organisms contaminated the sample.

Conclusion at the claimed species level: species-specific Pseudomonas CIP-10 support was not demonstrated. This remains an objective evidence conclusion, not an assigned significance bin or contamination-source category.

Other pilot results: Acetobacteroides and Tateyamaria had zero retained support against the selected references. Stenotrophomonas had zero retained support in round two. Miltoncostaea retained 11 competitive RNA reads covering only 130 reference bases, each 90 bp alignment with 7–11 edit differences. Its subsequent interval BLAST was skipped and is not presented as completed.

Specificity evidence · Per-alignment audit · Representative-pair BLAST · sucD-pair BLAST.

Assemblies actually analysed

The DNA SPAdes run used 5,685,476 cleaned pairs; RNA rnaSPAdes used 5,941,455 cleaned pairs. SPAdes4.2.0 is recorded in HPC logs. DNA assembly was not guided by the published reference. N50 is descriptive and does not establish correctness, completeness or contamination status.

Contig classification is overwhelmingly unclassified. Human-labelled DNA contigs and Bremia-labelled DNA/RNA sequences are provisional observations; no species-specific assembly validation has been performed for those labels. The DNA de novo assembly and the published assembly differ in size and fragmentation; differences can reflect assembly and curation rather than contamination.

Assembly depth retains MAPQ≥20 primary alignments. Unlike candidate depth, overlapping mates can both contribute. Repeated or shared transcript isoforms may lose support under this filter. RNA depth reflects expression, not genomic copy number. Contig taxonomy labels do not locate internal chimeric segments.

12

Independent public-genome FCS-GX case

Globisporangium irregulare strain 13-30, assembly GCA_051997085.1; BioProject PRJNA816194; BioSample SAMN26664723; WGS master JALBZS000000000. This is a third, assembly-only case, distinct from both original SRA readsets. No associated SRA run accession was verified; this does not establish that no reads are available.

Selection rationale: the user reports that NCBI flagged this genome as contaminated. The exact current flag wording was not independently retrieved. This is a deliberately selected, previously flagged case, not a blind discovery or a detection-limit experiment.

The supplied FCS-GX v0.5.0 action report classifies eight complete contigs as fungal Ascomycetes and recommends EXCLUDE. They total 12,358 bp, or 0.028973% of the 42,653,821 bp input assembly. The retained output has 5,443 sequences and 42,641,463 bp, versus 5,451 input sequences. Top taxon labels are provisional similarity assignments, not proof of living fungal associates or a particular contamination route.

No read fraction, sequencing depth or read-mapping breadth is available for this case. FCS alignment coverage and percentage of assembly bases are different measurements. Significance bins and likely sources remain student decisions. The original, retained and excluded FASTAs form an exact identifier partition, with sequence identity verified ignoring case. Cleaning converted lowercase sequence to uppercase, so soft-masking case was not preserved.

The original log records October 14, 2026 (timezone unspecified), database build January 24, 2023, and about 29,799 seconds (8.28 hours) processing. Job 102266 requested 40 GB and two CPUs; this is an allocation request, not measured peak memory or a general resource recommendation. No fresh container run was performed during this local integration.

Evidence: original action report; case interpretation and provenance; assembly detection table; portable Linux instructions; all datasets. NCBI linkage: BioProject assembly table. The seven embedded figures above belong to the original DNA/RNA branches; no BlobToolKit plot was supplied for this additional genome.

13

Interpretation, reproducibility and unfinished work

  • Noise, trace, consequential and biological bins remain the student’s decisions; source categories are not inferred automatically.
  • Human, fungal and other screening labels have not all undergone independent mapping validation.
  • FCS-GX completed for the additional G. irregulare genome only; no completed FCS report is retained for the original DNA/RNA assembly branches.
  • No DIAMOND viral-protein analysis, CheckV completeness result or independently validated RNA virus is reported.
  • No spike-in detection-limit experiment was performed.
  • The repository excludes raw reads and large regenerable intermediates. Compressed final assemblies, BlobDirs, tables, figures, software definitions and original logs are retained.
  • Historical completion markers describe the original HPC execution; removed intermediates and annotated source mean those markers must not be treated as current restart guarantees.
  • Archived original validation reports are distinguished from the fresh offline checks performed during repository curation.
